results.correct_value: NF-25 from Randle is paved; NF-28 (gravel) and NF-77 are the rough roads that want high clearance.
results.evidence: The Forest Service FR-28 page says FR-28 is paved only ~1.5 mi to the FR-76 junction, then gravel, not well maintained, high clearance recommended. Trailforks and a road-conditions site both describe NF-25 from Randle as a paved forest road (with deteriorated sections). The Pinto Rock area page calls NF-77 rough, go slow. So the hazard wrongly lumped NF-25 in with the rough gravel roads, and road.status's 'paved/maintained gravel' for NF-25 is tightened to 'paved'.

patches.find: Approach roads (NF-25/28/77) are rough gravel beyond the FR-76 junction and need a high-clearance vehicle.
patches.replace: Beyond paved NF-25, the approach roads (NF-28 and NF-77) are rough gravel and need a high-clearance vehicle.

patches.find: NF-25 is paved/maintained gravel for ~19 miles

results.evidence: The route's published pitch descriptions (P1 ramps to ledge, P2 groove and saddle traverse to chains, P3 up and right to semi-hanging belay, P4 up and left through basalt) do not say which pitches are hard to follow; no second source discusses route-finding on this line. Internally only the watch_out line and rope_note ('wandering P3/P4') point to the upper pitches, not enough to overrule obj_haz. A trip report naming the pitch where parties go off-route would settle it.

Sources give the climb as 400 ft (4 pitches) and the formation as just over 400 ft tall, but none states a car-to-car gain including the road walk from the pullout; the pullout elevation is not published. Per the rules gain_ft cannot be recomputed from waypoint arithmetic. A sourced pullout elevation or stated total gain would settle it.
